title: God is love
hook: a short letter answers what God is in three words

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Song of Songs: love set like a seal. Your line was many waters cannot quench love. Did that plain sentence get said out loud? Today, from the Hebrew Bible to the New Testament, and a three-word sentence. Day eight hundred thirty.

Ask a room of people what God is, and the answers get long fast. Maker of everything. Judge. Spirit. Mystery. Philosophers keep trying. Near the end of the New Testament there's a short letter, traditionally linked to the apostle John, that answers in three words. Not God has love, or God gives love, or God loves. Something stranger, and harder to get out of: God is love. Today, that sentence, and the test the same letter attaches to it.
screen: `WHAT IS GOD?` → `THE ANSWERS GET LONG.` → `A LETTER ANSWERS IN THREE WORDS.`

segments.voice: Here it is in the King James, in the fourth chapter of First John: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love." First, notice the shape. The letter doesn't say love is one of God's qualities, the way we'd say a person is tall or patient. It says God is love, as if love were what God is made of. Christian writers keep turning that over. Second, notice the problem the letter raises a few verses later: "No man hath seen God at any time." So how would anyone know God? The letter's answer: "If we love one another, God dwelleth in us." The unseen God shows up where people love each other. Third, the order. "We love him, because he first loved us." In this letter love doesn't start with us. It's received first, then passed on. Fourth, the test, and it's blunt. "If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar." The letter's reasoning is simple: if you can't love the brother you can see, how would you love God, whom you can't? So the sentence God is love isn't only a comfort. It's a measuring stick. Whatever else a reader believes about God, in this letter the sentence asks for something practical. In the letter's terms, love isn't proven in the sky. It's proven at the kitchen table, the office, the group chat, with the person right in front of you.
screen: `NOT GOD LOVES: GOD IS LOVE.` · `NO MAN HATH SEEN GOD.` · `WE LOVE, BECAUSE HE FIRST LOVED.` · `THE TEST: THE BROTHER YOU CAN SEE.` · then, large: `GOD IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Let one ordinary moment of today come to mind, something still ahead of you: a meeting, a meal, a drive, a conversation that usually goes sideways. Picture the person you'll see there. Now ask: what would it look like to act from love in that moment, just once? Not a feeling to force. An act. Listening to the end. Letting them go first. Saying thank you and meaning it. If you pray, you can rest in those three words from First John. If not, just rest with the person's face. The bell holds the time.
First John. The New Testament letter that answers what God is in three words, with a test attached: love the brother you can see. Today's word.
Your line: proven at the kitchen table. Today, in the moment you pictured, do the one loving act you chose, and notice what changes. Day eight hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Christians read First John in worship and private prayer, and the line God is love appears on church walls, cards and gravestones.
